olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Color positive integers blue or red so that the sum of any two same-colored numbers is blue. Find all valid colorings.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: From $k$ on the board, replace by $3k-1$, $2k+1$, or $k/2$ (if integer). Show any $n\geq 1$ can reach $3^{2023}$ in finitely many steps.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n=\overline{abcd}$ with $a\neq 0$ is \textit{guanaco} if $\overline{ab}\times\overline{cd}$ is a positive divisor of $n$. Find all guanaco numbers.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute $\triangle ABC$ with $AB<AC$, circumcircle $\Gamma$. $D$ = antipode of $A$ on $\Gamma$; $\ell$ = tangent at $D$. $P=BC\cap\ell$; $Q$ = second intersection of $AP$ with $\Gamma$; $R=QD\cap$ altitude from $A$. $S=AB\cap\ell$, $T=AC\cap\ell$. Show $S,T$ lie on the circumcircle of $\triangle AQR$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2023

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: $n\geq 3$ stones in a circle, labeled $1,\ldots,n$. Toads placed on stones; a toad on stone $k$ waits $k$ minutes then jumps clockwise. Find the maximum number of toads such that no two ever occupy the same stone simultaneously.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2023
